title: Data requirements and standardization
text: complete workflow illustrated follows. article focuses package’s data requirements first three steps, including functions Mapping(), DataCheck() DataStandard(). Two built-datasets included package. datasets stored data/ directory, scripts used generate provided data-raw/ directory. first dataset, BiSample, standardized longitudinal dataset satisfies package’s data requirements. contains nonstructural missing values; outcome values missing structurally unobservable due kind truncation. row represents one subject specific time. dataset includes subject identifier (id), assessment time (time), survival status (S), treatment assignment (), binary outcome (Y), six subject-level covariates (X1–X6) . second one, ImperfectConSample, designed resemble longitudinal data collected clinical trial repeated follow-assessments. row represents patient observation scheduled visit. dataset includes patient identifier (patient_id), visit time (visit_month), survival status (alive_status), treatment assignment (treatment), continuous clinical outcome, six patient-level covariates (X1–X6) representing relevant clinical demographic information.

title: Data requirements and standardization
text: Mapping() sole source truth structural columns, analysis window raw time scale, covariated used estimate treatment effects, variables interest, outcome type. arguments id, time, treatment, survival, outcome specify corresponding column names input dataset. arguments baseline_time cutoff_time define beginning end analysis window, respectively. must specified single finite numeric value raw time scale, baseline_time < cutoff_time. example, obeserved time points (0, 1, …, 4) may set 0 1, whereas cutoff may set later time point, 4. ImperfectConSample, observed time points (0, 6, 12); therefore, analysis window defined using baseline_time = 0, cutoff_time = 12. argument covariates interest_vars character vectors containing column names relevant covariates. Variables specified interest_vars must also included covariates . argument y_type specifies outcome type. set B binary outcome C continuous outcome. Users can inspect mapping details using print() attributes() function may additionally used inspect object-level metadata, class.

title: Diagnostics, profiling, and sensitivity analysis
text: PSDiag() uses original pooled denominator weighting weighted effective-sample-size denominator ordinary IPTW. weights calculated, always executes pi <- pmin(pmax(pi, 0.01), 0.99).
code: ps_diag <- PSDiag(pd_data, ps_fo) ps_diag$smd_before ps_diag$smd_after ps_diag$weights ps_diag$propensity plot(ps_diag)

title: Diagnostics, profiling, and sensitivity analysis
text: PrinSDiag() evaluates original diagnostic equation cutoff using cumulative principal probabilities. propensity scores also always clipped [0.01, 0.99] diagnostic denominators formed.
code: prin_diag <- PrinSDiag(pd_data, ps_fo, prin_fo) prin_diag$statistics prin_diag$p0 prin_diag$p1 prin_diag$propensity plot(prin_diag)

title: Diagnostics, profiling, and sensitivity analysis
text: observed time, SA() defines perturbation variance using ordinary variance observed outcomes time. Binary analyses retain binomial logistic nuisance model use bounded-link HTE equation; continuous analyses retain original linear-model closed-form equations.
code: set.seed(20260728) binary_sa <- SA(   pd_data,   A ~ X1 + X2 + X4,   S ~ X1 + X2 + X4 + A + time,   Y ~ X1 + X2 + A,   ratiovec = c(0, 0.02) )  data("ImperfectConSample", package = "PDRobust") continuous_map <- Mapping(   id = "patient_id",   time = "visit_month",   treatment = "treatment",   survival = "alive_status",   outcome = "clinical_outcome",   baseline_time = 0,   cutoff_time = 12,   covariates = paste0("X", 1:6),   interest_vars = c("X1", "X2"),   y_type = "C" ) continuous_data <- DataStandard(   ImperfectConSample, continuous_map, drop = TRUE )  continuous_sa <- SA(   continuous_data,   treatment ~ X1 + X2 + X4,   alive_status ~ X1 + X2 + X4 + treatment + visit_month,   clinical_outcome ~ X1 + X2 + treatment,   ratiovec = c(0, 0.05) )  binary_sa$data continuous_sa$data

title: Getting started with PDRobust
text: Mapping() returns pd_mapping. DataCheck() returns pd_data_check report without modifying data. DataStandard() returns pd_data frame standardized mapping, ID/time maps, readiness checks, attrition audit stored attributes.
code: library(PDRobust)  data("BiSample", package = "PDRobust") raw <- BiSample map <- Mapping(   id = "id",   time = "time",   treatment = "A",   survival = "S",   outcome = "Y",   baseline_time = 0,   cutoff_time = 2,   covariates = c("X1", "X2", "X4"),   interest_vars = c("X1", "X2"),   y_type = "B" )  check <- DataCheck(raw, map) check$ready_for_analysis check$checks  pd_data <- DataStandard(raw, map) standardized_map <- attr(pd_data, "pd_mapping")

title: Getting started with PDRobust
text: prediction function refits model fit_dat returns numeric pd_prediction vector aligned pred_dat.
code: ps_fo <- A ~ X1 + X2 + X4 prin_fo <- S ~ X1 + X2 + X4 + A + time out_fo <- Y ~ X1 + X2 + A  ps <- PSPred(ps_fo, pd_data, pd_data, standardized_map) p0 <- PrinPred(prin_fo, pd_data, pd_data, 0, standardized_map) p1 <- PrinPred(prin_fo, pd_data, pd_data, 1, standardized_map) mu1 <- OutPred(   out_fo,   pd_data[pd_data$S == 1, , drop = FALSE],   pd_data,   a = 1,   mapping = standardized_map )  head(cbind(ps, p0, p1, mu1))

title: Independent prediction models
text: multiple observed times, baseline rows excluded principal model’s risk set. post-baseline row fitted survival immediately preceding observed time equals one. Conditional predictions baseline set one accumulated within subject complete baseline--cutoff grid. single observed time, -risk indicator constructed complete rows used. Separation, aliased nuisance coefficients, extreme fitted probabilities may produce warnings. invalidate prediction fitted model still returns complete finite vector. Missing, non-finite, row-misaligned predictions remain errors. Direct prediction functions report one normalized warning per fit. HTESepT(), HTEAllT(), SA() consolidate repeated point-estimate warnings retain bootstrap warnings returned diagnostics. Within one analysis sample, fitted principal-score outcome model reused two counterfactual treatment predictions fitting rows formula identical. Public prediction vectors rounded three decimal places. Analysis functions call full-precision internal implementations, display rounding never enters weights, estimating equations, optimization, bootstrap replicates, confidence-interval calculations.

title: PDRobust

code: # \donttest{ data("BiSample", package = "PDRobust") map <- Mapping(   id = "id", time = "time", treatment = "A",   survival = "S", outcome = "Y",   baseline_time = 0, cutoff_time = 2,   covariates = c("X1", "X2", "X4"),   interest_vars = c("X1", "X2"), y_type = "B" ) pd_dat <- DataStandard(BiSample, map) result <- SA(   pd_dat,   A ~ X1 + X2 + X4,   S ~ X1 + X2 + X4 + A + time,   Y ~ X1 + X2 + A,   ratiovec = c(0, 0.05) ) head(result$data) #>   ratio time      term estimate #> 1     0    0 Intercept    0.225 #> 2     0    0        X1   -0.041 #> 3     0    0        X2   -0.070 #> 4     0    1 Intercept   -0.244 #> 5     0    1        X1   -0.385 #> 6     0    1        X2    0.233 # }
